name: Water (Drinking/Mineral)
imageAlt: a glass of clean, pure drinking water
description: Water ($H_2O$) is the non-negotiable molecular foundation for all terrestrial life, acting as the universal biological solvent and thermodynamic regulator. It is engineered to drive systemic cellular hydration, facilitate metabolic waste clearance via renal pathways, balance intracellular fluid homeostasis, and serve as a pristine transport matrix for essential trace elements.
macroIntro: An inert, calorically neutral solvent containing zero protein, fat, or carbohydrates.
microIntro: While organic-free, mineral-rich water provides bioavailable inorganic electrolytes essential for cellular function.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Zero energy density; ideal for sustaining hydration without metabolic loading.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: Inorganic ionic fraction supporting skeletal density and muscular signaling.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Electrolyte assisting in vascular relaxation and cardiovascular electrical stability.

microNutrients.name: Sodium
microNutrients.description: Extracellular electrolyte coordinating osmotic pressure and nerve impulse kinetics.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: Intracellular electrolyte essential for membrane potential and fluid homeostasis.

healthBenefits: Cellular Hydration: Maintains intracellular volume and membrane plasticity, critical for enzymatic activity.
Waste Clearance: Optimizes glomerular filtration (GFR) for the systematic removal of urea and metabolites.
Thermoregulation: Preserves core homeostatic temperature via perspiration and heat dissipation.
Vascular Volume: Stabilizes blood plasma volume, modulating viscosity and cardiac workload.
Lubrication: Forms the structural basis of synovial and mucosal fluids, reducing mechanical wear.
precautions: Hyponatremia: Excessive rapid intake exceeds renal excretion, diluting extracellular sodium and causing cerebral edema.
Mineral Saturation: Highly mineralized (high-TDS) water may strain filtration pathways if consumed exclusively.
Biological Contamination: Unfiltered sources carry risks of pathogens, heavy metals, and microplastics.
